CEQA (California Environmental Quality Act):

on the environment.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

Pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code ("MPMC") § 4.30.150, the City may
recover abatement-related costs by recording a special assessment upon real
property located at 229 E. Markland Drive. The City has incurred abatement-related
costs totaling $124,715.14. A special assessment for abatement related costs was
previously recorded in the amount of $52,510.03, leaving a balance of $72,205.11.
The property owner is deceased and the heirs to the estate have been absent from
the legal proceedings and excused by the Court, obviating the need to provide an
opportunity to either remit payment to the City or contest the costs incurred. This
Resolution seeks another special assessment on the Property for the balance of
abatement costs incurred by the City in the amount of $72,205.11.

 BACKGROUND:

 I.  Nuisance Enforcement, Abatement and Cost Recovery, Generally.

 The MPMC authorizes the City to engage in nuisance abatement when private
 property owners refuse to voluntarily bring their properties into compliance.
 Abatement costs include the time spent and actions performed in furtherance of
 abating public nuisances.

 Government Code § 39773.5 and MPMC § 4.39.150 allow the City to place a lien
 upon real property to recover any unpaid enforcement/abatement costs incurred
 by the City. If such a special assessment is unpaid after three years, the tax
 collector may sell the property to recover the total amount owed.

II.  229 E. Markland Drive

  A.  Prior Abatement and Special Assessment

 229 E. Markland Drive, Assessor’s Parcel Number 5265-007-007, is a detached, single
 family, residential property (“Property”). In the summer of 2018, the City began to receive
 complaints regarding overgrown vegetation and inoperable vehicles at the front of the
 property; it had also come to the City's attention that the property lacked running water
 for some time. The City's Code Enforcement and Building Divisions subsequently
 inspected the interior and exterior of the property on December 19, 2018 and confirmed,
 among other things, the lack of running water to the property, the storage of junk,
 abandoned personal property and refuse, and overgrown vegetation amounting to
 hoarder conditions; the property was subsequently "red tagged." This ultimately led to
 several abatement actions by the City to address conditions on the exterior of the property
 and squatters setting fires on the interior which amounted to an immediate threat to public
 health and safety, as well as a blight to the community.

 City abatement costs totaling $52,510.03 were properly noticed to the property
 owner/heirs. On August 19, 2020, the City Council adopted Resolution 12189 to Record
 a Notice of Special Assessment for Nuisance Abatement at 229 E. Markland Drive for
 $52,510.03, which was subsequently recorded by the County on April 1, 2021.

  B.  Subsequent Receivership Action

 The City later learned that the owner of the Property, Mary Perez, had died intestate
 and her remaining heirs either could not be located or disavowed any interest in the
 Property. While junk, trash and debris from the exterior of the property had been
 cleaned up, the Property remained a blight to the neighborhood and the interior
 Staff Report

contained profound hoarding conditions of more trash, junk, and biological matter
filling it three feet or more above the floor.

On September 18, 2020, the City Attorney, on behalf of the People of the State of
California, filed a receivership action in Los Angeles Superior Court case no.
20GDCV00721, seeking a court-appointed receiver to completely rehabilitate the
Property and act as the official representative of the Property in all respects. The
court granted the City’s motion to appoint a receiver on May 28, 2021.

In November 2022, the court-appointed receiver completed a full rehabilitation of the
Property, and subsequently listed it for sale with the intention that proceeds would
pay for the receiver’s rehabilitation and costs, the City’s abatement-related costs, and
outstanding third-party debts secured by the Property, as authorized by the court.
Offers to purchase the Property are currently under consideration.

  C.  Current Abatement Costs

On December 8, 2022, the City Attorney’s office submitted to the Receiver a total
demand of abatement-related costs totaling $122,545.14, satisfying the notice
requirement to the Property representative (attached as “Attachment 2,” and
incorporated by reference), and which was incorporated as an exhibit into Receiver’s
Motion for Sale of the Property. Since that submission through January 31, 2023, the
City has accrued an additional $2,170.00 in legal fees, bringing the current total to
$124,715.14 (attached as “Attachment 3,” and incorporated by reference).

A special assessment in the amount of $52,510.03 covering expenses up through
August 2020 was previously recorded (attached as “Attachment 4,” and incorporated
by reference)., leaving a balance of $72,205.11. Recording a special assessment in
the amount of $72,205.11 is necessary to help ensure the City’s priority in recovering
its abatement-related costs from the sale of the Property through receivership
proceedings.

FISCAL IMPACT:

This Resolution will allow the City to recover $72,205.11.

  nuisance abatement at that address. The assessment of $52,510.03 was
  subsequently recorded against the property on April 1, 2021.

  C.  On September 18, 2020, the City Attorney, on behalf of the People of the
  State of California, filed a receivership action in Los Angeles Superior Court

  rehabilitate the Property and act as the official representative of the Property
  in all respects. The court granted the City’s motion to appoint a receiver on
  May 28, 2021.

  D.  In November 2022, the court-appointed receiver completed a full
  rehabilitation of the Property, and subsequently listed it for sale with the
  intention that proceeds would pay for the receiver’s rehabilitation and costs,
  the City’s abatement-related costs, and outstanding third-party debts
  secured by the Property, as authorized by the court. Offers to purchase the
  Property are currently under consideration.

  E.  On December 8, 2022, the City Attorney’s office submitted to the Receiver
  a total demand of abatement-related costs totaling $122,545.14, satisfying

  incorporated as an exhibit into Receiver’s Motion for Sale of the Property.

  from the sale of the Property through receivership proceedings.

  G.  Pursuant to Government Code § 38773.5 and Monterey Park Municipal
  Code § 4.30.150, the City may make costs related to abatement of
  nuisances a special assessment against a parcel.

SECTION 2: The City Council finds that all notices required by the Government Code
and MPMC were provided to recover all abatement costs owed to the City. The City
Council approves, confirms, and adopts the Notice attached as Attachment 2 and
determines that each such charge is proper and correct. Such charges constitute a lien
on the real property upon which the public nuisance was abated and will be collected as
a special assessment against the real property.

SECTION 3: The City Clerk is directed to:

  A.  Mail a copy of the Notice of Abatement Costs attached in Attachment 2 to
  the Receiver, acting on behalf of the property owner, pursuant to MPMC §
  4.20.150(b);

  B.  File a certified copy of this Resolution (with attachments) with the Los
  Angeles County Assessor and Treasurer and Tax Collector;

  C.  Submit a certified copy of this Resolution (with attachments) with the Los
  Angeles County Recorder for recordation, pursuant to Government Code §
  38773.5;

  D.  Direct the Los Angeles County Assessor to enter the amount of the charge
  against the real property described in this Resolution on the current
  assessment rolls; and

  E.  Take any other action necessary to effectuate this Resolution.

SECTION 4: The Los Angeles County Assessor and Treasurer and Tax Collector are
requested to add the amount of the assessment to the next regular tax bill levied against
the property for municipal purposes.

SECTION 5: This Resolution does not affect any penalty, forfeiture or liability incurred
before, or preclude prosecution and imposition of penalties for any violation incurring
before, this Resolution’s effective date. Any such amendment part will remain in full force
and effect for sustaining action or prosecuting violations occurring before the effective
date of this Resolution.

SECTION 6: If any part of this Resolution or its application is deemed invalid by a court
of competent jurisdiction, the City Council intends that such invalidity will not affect the

  The City Council of the City of Monterey Park does resolve as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds and declares that:

  A  229 E. Markland Drive is located in the City of Monterey Park, State of
  California, and more particularly described as Assessor's Parcel Number
  5265-007 -007 (" P roperty" ) ;

  B.  On July 3, 2019, the Property was declared to be a public nuisance; the
  City later abated the nuisance pursuant to an abatement warrant issued
  by the Los Angeles County Superior Court (dated July 24, 2019). The
  Property owner was notified of the issuance of the abatement warrant and
  the exterior of the Property was abated between August 2nd and August
  7th, 2019. The costs incurred by the City for this abatement totaled
  $36,047.63;

  c  On April 11, 2020, the Monterey Park Police (MPPD) and Fire
  Departments (MPFD) were called to the Property. Upon arrival, MPPD
  observed evidence that persons were squatting within both the detached
  garage and dwelling; and MPFD was required to put out a fire that had
  been lit within the dwelling. At the scene, MPPD also found evidence that
  the fuse box on the property had been rewired and that wires have been
  connected directly to the powerlines servicing the dwelling;

  D.  On April 15, 2020, the City Manager signed an Order for Urgency
  Abatement at the property to immediately abate the public nuisance on the
  property. This order was ratified by the City Council on May 6, 2020. The
  Property was abated on or about April 17,2020, by (1) ensuring that the
  structures on the Property were vacant; (2) putting out the fire within the
  dwelling on the Property; (3) securing the vacanUabandoned dwelling and
  accessory structure against criminal activity, vandalism, on-site loitering
  and any other attractive nuisances by enclosing the perimeter of the
  Property with a padlocked chain-link fence; and (4) clearing the Property
  of overgrown vegetation that constituted afire hazard. The costs incurred
  by the City for this abatement total $16,462.40;

  E  The City incurred a total of $ 52,510.03 in costs abating the public
  nuisance. An itemized Notice of Abatement Costs letter for work
  performed by the City was provided to the property owner on June 15,
  2020 ("Notice");

  SPECIAL MEETING
  FEBRUARY 15, 2023

The City Council, the Financing Authority (MPFA), the Housing Authority (MPHA), the
Geologic Hazard Abatement District (GHAD), and the Successor Agency (SA) of the
City of Monterey Park held a Special Meeting of the Council in Room 266, located at
320 West Newmark Avenue in the City of Monterey Park, Wednesday, February 15,
2023 at 5:30 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER:
Mayor Sanchez called the meeting to order at 5:35 p.m.

ROLL CALL:
Mayor Sanchez called the roll:

Council Members Present:  Henry Lo, Yvonne Yiu, Vinh Ngo, Thomas Wong, Jose
  Sanchez
Council Members Absent:  None

ALSO PRESENT: City Attorney Karl Berger and Deputy City Clerk Cindy Trang

ORAL AND WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS: None.

1.  OPEN SESSION

1-A.  CONSIDERATION AND POSSIBLE ACTION TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO
  RECORD A NOTICE OF SPECIAL ASSESSMENT FOR NUISANCE
  ABATEMENT AT 229 E. MARKLAND DRIVE (APN 5265-007-007)

  Pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code ("MPMC") § 4.30.150, the City may
  recover abatement-related costs by recording a special assessment upon real
  property located at 229 E. Markland Drive. The City has incurred abatement-
  related costs totaling $124,715.14. A special assessment for abatement related
  costs was previously recorded in the amount of $52,510.03, leaving a balance of
  $72,205.11. The property owner is deceased and the heirs to the estate have
  been absent from the legal proceedings and excused by the Court, obviating the
  need to provide an opportunity to either remit payment to the City or contest the
  costs incurred. This Resolution seeks another special assessment on the

  Act (“CEQA”) under CEQA Guidelines § 15061(b)(3) because it can be seen with

  effect on the environment.

  Action Taken: The City Council adopted Resolution No. 2023-R9 to record a
  Notice of Special Assessment for Nuisance Abatement.
